 Judgment

This is an appeal under section 29 of The Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005, (
in short PWDV Act) filed by the Appellant/husband challenging the orders dated 02.02.2024 passed by Learned MMTC - I, Bangalore in Crl. Misc.172/2015, partly allowing the petition under section 12 of the PWDV Act and restraining the Appellant/husband herein aiding, abetting and causing act of Mohammed Muzaffar vs Balquees Banu on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131654631/
1 domestic violence, to pay maintenance of Rs.5,000/- per month to the petitioner towards food,
shelter and clothing from the date of petition till her life time or till she she remarries and Rs.3,000/- per month to the child Mohammed Rehan from the date of petition till he attains majority and to bear the educational expenses of said child and to secure alternative accommodation to the respondent/wife or pay rent and also to pay Rs.50,000/- as compensation.
2.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the memorandum of appeal is as under:
The marriage between the respondent and appellant took place on 05.11.2012 at Bangalore as per the CRL.A. No.25114/2024 Mohammedan Law.
At the time of marriage the appellant demanded dowry of Rs.3 lakhs and gold ornaments and household articles.
However, the father of Petitioner expressing his inability has given Rs.1 Lakh and gold ornaments like two gold chain and household articles by bearing the marriage expenses.
3. It is the further case of the respondent/wife that out of the wedlock male child was born on 11.08.2013 named as Mohammed Rehan who is under the care and custody of the respondent/wife.
The appellant and his family members used to assault the respondent and demanded to bring more dowry from her parents.
The appellant was not providing any food, clothes and medicines to the respondent/wife.
Accordingly the respondent/wife lodged police complaint against appellant/husband and his family members on 10.12.2014, 22.12.2014, 24.03.2015.

Thereafter,
police have registered Crime No.37/2015 against CRL.A. No.25114/2024 appellant/husband for the offence punishable u/sec.506, 498A of IPC r/w Sec. 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The appellant/husband and his family members have assaulted and thrown the respondent / wife out of the house demanding to bring more money.
Since 11.08.2013 the respondent / wife is residing with her parents in her parents house.
The appellant / husband and his family members never made any efforts to take back the respondent/wife.
The appellant / husband also threatened the respondent with dire consequences.
The appellant / husband is doing finance and getting income of Rs.35,000/- per month and also getting rental income of Rs.45,000/- per month.
The appellant/husband completely neglected the respondent/wife and child without any reason.

4. After registering the case the trial court issued notice to appellant/husband herein and he appeared before the trial court through his counsel and he filed his CRL.A. No.25114/2024 objection admitting his marriage with respondent/wife and also the respondent/wife given birth to male child.
He also admitted that Crime No.37/2015 is registered against him.
However, he denied other averments of the petition and prays to dismiss the petition.
5. The respondent/wife so as to prove her case got examined herself as PW-1 before the trial court and she has not produced any document.
The appellant/husband not entered into witness box and not produced any documents.
After hearing the arguments of both sides the learned Magistrate passed the impugned order on 02.02.2024.

The appellant/husband being aggrieved by the said order filed the present appeal on the following Grounds:
Mohammed Muzaffar vs Balquees Banu on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131654631/
2 1.

sentences.text: That the impugned order dated 02.02.2024 is perverse, capricious against to the principles of natural justice.
The trial court grossly erred in understanding the case of the appellant/husband.
The trial court has CRL.A. No.25114/2024 not considered that the respondent/wife not approached the court with clean hands.
2. The marriage between the appellant/husband and respondent/wife took place on 05.11.2012 as per Mohammedan Law.
Out of their wedlock a male child was born on 11.08.2013.
He denied that he demanded dowry and also gold ornaments and household articles.
3. He is not capable to pay separate maintenance to the respondent/wife.
It is the father of respondent/wife was torturing through anti-social elements and police.
He has not received any gold jewelry as alleged.
The trial court has no jurisdiction to grant order u/sec.23 of PWDV Act.
4. He was not provided with opportunity to cross-examine the respondent/wife.
The respondent/wife also had one more maintenance case before the family court.
The said fact is suppressed by the respondent/wife.
He is earning meager salary of Rs.6,000/- per month.
The impugned order is required to be modified, the appeal is filed within the period of limitation.
Accordingly prays CRL.A. No.25114/2024 to allow the appeal and to set aside the order and to remand the matter by giving him an opportunity to cross- examine the respondent/wife.
6. In pursuance to issuance of court notice, the respondent/wife appeared through her counsel and contested the appeal and prays to dismiss the appeal.

7. Heard arguments of both the appellant and the respondent and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

The points that would arise for my consideration are:
1. Whether the impugned order requires to be set aside?
2. What order?
9. My answer on the aforesaid points are as under:-
Point No.1: In the Negative Point No.2:As per the final order, for the following:-
CRL.A. No.25114/2024 REASONS 10. POINT No.1: In the case on hand it is not in dispute that the respondent/wife is the legally wedded wife of appellant/husband and out of their wedlock the respondent/wife given birth to a Mohammed Muzaffar vs Balquees Banu on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131654631/
3 male child.
11.
It is necessary to note that the appellant/husband not denied the fact of registering FIR in crime No.37/2015 against him for the offence punishable u/sec.,506, 498A of IPC r/w sec. 3 & 4 of DP Act.

It is necessary to note that argument of the appellant/husband is that the respondent/wife herself deserted him and he cannot make arrangement of alternative or separate residence as he is earning meager income and he cannot pay maintenance.

12. It is necessary to note that this respondent/wife in her affidavit of assets and liabilities stated that she has studied up to SSLC, the appellant/husband is bus driver CRL.A. No.25114/2024 and earning Rs.50,000/- per month and also owns residential properties worth Rs.2 crores.
13. The appellant/husband in his affidavit of assets and liabilities before the trial court stated that he has studied 8th standard and he is driver by profession.
He shown his mother as dependent.
He shown his monthly income as Rs.6,000/-.
14. It is not in dispute that presently the respondent/ wife is living with her parents.
It is also not disputed that the minor child Mohammed Rehan is in the custody of this respondent/wife.
The appellant/husband has not taken any such defence that the respondent/wife is capable of earning herself and can maintain herself.
It is also not the defence of this appellant/husband that the parents of the respondent/wife are capable to look after the respondent/ wife and minor child.
It is not in dispute that the appellant/husband and respondent/wife lived together as husband and wife in a shared household.
The contention of the appellant/husband is that he has not given with opportunity to cross-examine PW-1.

In this regard on perusal of the trial court records this respondent/wife got examined herself as PW-1 on 15.04.2017 and thereafter on 27.09.2018 the case was posted for cross-examination of PW-1 and this appellant/husband was given with opportunity to cross- examine PW-1 from 16.11.2018 to 26.10.2021.
It is almost morethan 2  years the case was posted for cross- examination of PW-1 and the appellant/husband not chosen to cross-examine PW-1.
That apart on the basis of application to recall the PW-1 for cross-examination PW-1 was recalled and even thereafter this appellant/husband not chosen to cross-examine PW-1.
It is on 12.06.2023 cross-examination of PW-1 was taken as nil.
Again on the basis of application of appellant/husband to recall PW-1 this PW-1 was recalled and even then this PW-1 was not cross

-examined and even this appellant / husband not complied the order of trial court to pay the 50% of the CRL.A.
No.25114/2024 arrears of maintenance ordered to the respondent/wife.
Hence, the contention of the appellant/husband that he was not given with sufficient opportunity to cross-examine PW-1 cannot be accepted.
16. That apart on perusal of the appeal memo the present appeal is filed on 19.03.2024.
The impugned order challenged in this appeal is dated 02.02.2024.
Admittedly there is delay of 17 days.

On perusal of the certified copy of the order produced by the appellant/husband it shows that the Mohammed Muzaffar vs Balquees Banu on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131654631/
4 appellant/husband applied for certified copy of order on 13.02.2024 and the appellant/husband was directed to appear on 03.03.2024.
However, the copy was taken by the appellant/husband on 22.02.2024 itself.
The appeal should have been filed on or before 03.03.2024.
The present appeal is filed on 19.03.2024.

If the time spent in obtaining the copy of the order is excluded ie., if 10 days is excluded then also the appeal is filed after 7 days of the prescribed period hence there is 7 days delay in filing this CRL.A. No.25114/2024 appeal.
However, the appellant not filed any application for condoning the delay.
Hence, the appeal is not maintainable 17.

That apart even the appeal is considered on merits this appellant/husband who is duty bound husband has not taken least risk to take back his wife and minor child and not provided any accommodation and though he was driver by profession not placed any evidence to disbelieve the case of the petitioner in respect of his monthly income.
Accordingly, the learned trial court by considering the oral as well as documentary evidence of both the parties and by considering the entire records passed the impugned order.
The impugned order is one such order, interference of this court in the order passed by the learned Magistrate will not arise.

Accordingly, I answer point for consideration No.1 in Negative and proceed to pass the following:-
CRL.A. No.25114/2024 ORDER
Appeal filed by the appellant is hereby dismissed.
Send the copy of this order along with trial court records to the trial court.
No order as to costs.
